findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add the pinned help contract (src/rebar/_cli/help/bridge.txt) and the hardcoded metavar in _bridge_commands.py:_parser to the scope so the new `projects` verb appears in the bridge group's byte-exact help.
evidence: _help.py:52 subcommand_help loads the pinned bridge.txt verbatim as a contract ('byte-for-byte copies')
Scope names _cli/_bridge_commands.py but not the help/bridge.txt package-data file
findings.finding: The plan adds a `projects` verb to the bridge verb group but does not enumerate the pinned byte-exact help contract that lists the group's commands. src/rebar/_cli/help/bridge.txt currently lists only `preview` and `sync` and is served verbatim via _help.subcommand_help; adding a verb without updating it leaves the pinned help out of sync (and any parity/golden test over it would fail).
findings.location: Scope section (files list) / Approach ('bridge projects under the verb group')
scenarios: `rebar bridge` (bare group) or `rebar help bridge` renders pinned text that omits the new `projects` command
a golden/parity test over pinned help vs. argparse output fails

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether `set <KEY>` replaces or merges the repos list for an already-present key (recommend: replace).
evidence: The plan defines `set <KEY> --repos a,b` and an edge case for empty `--repos`, but never states whether re-running `set` on an existing key replaces the repos list or merges into it.
findings.finding: The `set` sub-verb's overwrite-vs-merge semantics on an already-present key are unspecified.
scenarios: Operator runs `set REB --repos rebar` then later `set REB --repos other` — does REB now map to [other] or [rebar, other]?
findings.suggested_fix: Add: 'set replaces the entry wholesale — the stored repos list becomes exactly the passed --repos value.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the module choice with parent 0e68's file_impact: either note in the leaf that the new projects_store.py supersedes the parent's binding_store.py hint (updating the parent), or confirm the parent intends the mapping code to live in a dedicated module so the two plans agree.
evidence: Leaf Approach: 'owned by a new projects_store.py module rather than by extending binding_store.py'
Parent 0e68 file_impact: path 'src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py', reason 'store-level project->repos mapping lives beside the existing shared bridge state'
Parent AC-1 only constrains the on-disk location (.bridge_state/projects.json), not the owning module — so the deliverable is preserved and this mismatch is cosmetic (incomplete_enumeration)
findings.finding: The parent (0e68) file_impact places the store-level project->repos mapping in src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py ('store-level project->repos mapping lives beside the existing shared bridge state'), whereas this leaf explicitly declines to extend binding_store.py and introduces a new src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/projects_store.py module. The parent's binding acceptance criterion only requires the record at .bridge_state/projects.json (which the leaf honors), so this is an implementation-level refinement, not a contract contradiction — but the wording diverges from the parent's named file.
findings.location: Approach / Scope — 'projects_store.py (new)' vs parent 0e68 file_impact binding_store.py
scenarios: A parent-vs-leaf file-ownership cross-check flags the mapping as living in a different module than the parent named
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to the leaf's Approach noting that the parent's binding_store.py file_impact entry is superseded by the dedicated projects_store.py module (the record location .bridge_state/projects.json is unchanged), and/or update parent 0e68's file_impact accordingly.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how `legacy_default` is created/edited (a verb or documented default) and add a criterion that exercises it.
evidence: Record shape includes '"legacy_default": "REB"'; resolve_project AC says 'returns the legacy default for an absent field'; but sub-verbs are only 'list', 'set <KEY> --repos', 'remove <KEY>' — none set legacy_default, and no AC covers populating it.
findings.finding: `legacy_default` is part of the record shape and is consumed by `resolve_project`, but no verb or criterion writes or edits it.
findings.location: Record shape / Sub-verbs / AC for resolve_project
scenarios: Operator needs to change which project pre-epic tickets resolve to and finds no CLI path; tests never write legacy_default so its read path is unexercised except as a literal.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add `set --legacy-default <KEY>` (or a `--legacy-default` flag) and a covering AC, or state that legacy_default is seeded once at store init with a fixed value and add a test asserting resolve_project reads it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the write is atomic (temp-file + rename) and note the consume-vs-edit ordering assumption for in-flight passes.
evidence: 'The `projects` key set is the store's sync list' — so passes consume it while operators mutate it via set/remove.
No mention of atomic write (temp-file rename) or of what a pass sees if it reads mid-edit.
findings.finding: projects.json is read by every sync pass (it IS the sync list) yet operator-editable via the CLI; the plan does not address atomic writes or concurrent-edit-vs-in-flight-pass safety.
scenarios: An operator runs `bridge projects remove REB` while a sync pass is reading projects.json — pass reads a partially-written or truncated file.
Crash mid-write leaves projects.json corrupt, breaking every subsequent pass.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Approach: 'projects_store writes via temp-file-and-rename so a reader always sees a complete record; concurrent operator edits and passes are serialized at the file level.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that projects_store.py persists via the existing rebar._store.fsutil.atomic_write helper (canonical json.dump with sort_keys/indent) rather than re-open-coding the tempfile+os.replace dance.
evidence: binding_store.py:292-314 open-codes tempfile.mkstemp + os.replace for its atomic save
src/rebar/_store/fsutil.py:48 defines a reusable atomic_write(path, data, ...) with the same temp-in-same-dir + os.replace semantics
The plan's byte-identical/byte-unchanged test invariants imply atomic, canonical JSON writes but name no persist helper
findings.finding: The new projects_store.py will persist JSON to disk, but the plan does not say to reuse the existing atomic-write helper; the tempfile+os.replace persist dance is already open-coded in binding_store.save() and packaged reusably as rebar._store.fsutil.atomic_write.
scenarios: projects_store re-implements a third copy of the atomic JSON-write logic instead of calling the shared helper
findings.suggested_fix: Note in Approach that the store's write path calls rebar._store.fsutil.atomic_write with a canonical JSON serialization, matching binding_store's format, so the byte-stability invariants hold and no new persist code is introduced.

findings.checklist_item: State that projects_store persists projects.json atomically (e.g. tempfile + os.replace, matching binding_store.save()), so a crash or concurrent edit cannot leave a torn record.
evidence: binding_store.save() at binding_store.py:292 uses mkstemp + os.replace for atomic bindings.json writes ('atomically replace bindings with safe fallback state')
The plan states set/remove verbs write .bridge_state/projects.json but never names how the write is made durable/atomic against a crash or concurrent operator edit
The record is committed store state shared by every repo, so a torn write is a correctness hazard, not just cosmetic
findings.finding: The plan does not specify the write mechanism (atomicity / partial-write safety) for projects.json, though the sibling binding_store.save() persists via tempfile + os.replace.
scenarios: Process killed mid-write during 'bridge projects set' leaves a truncated projects.json that every repo then fails to parse
Two concurrent operator edits race on the same file
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Approach: projects_store writes projects.json via the same atomic tempfile+os.replace pattern binding_store.save() uses, so a mapping write is all-or-nothing.
